rows.evidence: The .catch arrow at goal-fan-out-driver.ts:218 is the rejection handler of the promise returned by work.finally(...). track has exactly two callers (grep `track(`): the re-entry IIFE, whose whole body is inside try/catch/finally (:289-300, catch :294-295, finally :296-298), and fanOut's runPass (:491). runPass catches the live-runs read (:404-409), every fanOutRun (:421-425) and the resume-continuations read (:443-448); the only unguarded remainder is controlOf (:412-413) and deps.driving(), which production supplies as `() => leaseOwned` (host.ts:589), a captured boolean. So neither tracked promise can reject and the arm is never entered.
rows.proposal_note: Deleting the catch, keeping `void work.finally(() => into.delete(work))`, still removes the work from the set. It is also the only consumer of the finally promise, so a future unexpected throw would turn into an unhandled rejection; keeping the line untested (claude's alternative) is the cheaper option.

rows.evidence: The arrow at goal-fan-out-driver.ts:514 is the rejection handler of fanOut. fanOut is `track(runPass({ ...ctx, signal: hostSignal }, ...), passes)` (:490-492), and runPass cannot reject: the reads are inside try/catch (:404-409, :443-448), each fanOutRun is inside a try (:420-426), and driving is `() => leaseOwned` in the only production assembly (host.ts:584-589). checkWatches (:495-516) is the only caller that adds this catch, and its own caller guards it again (:525).
rows.proposal_note: `await fanOut(...)` is behaviourally identical; the catch never fires. Same unhandled-rejection caveat as C3-016, so keep-untested is acceptable too.

rows.evidence: The arrow at goal-fan-out-driver.ts:525 is the rejection handler of checkWatches. Its body (:495-516) awaits only setImmediate (:497), wraps each controls.readControl in try/catch (:501-506), and the rest is Map delete/set (:508-510); the one fanOut call carries its own catch (:512-515). So checkWatches cannot reject; scheduleCheck (:522-526) is its only caller and the arm is never entered.
rows.proposal_note: `await checkWatches()` is equivalent. Since this arrow also protects the scheduleCheck drain loop from poisoning, keeping it untested (claude's option) is defensible instead of deleting.

rows.evidence: grep over src and tests: the registry's `currentVersion` has only the interface member (host-settings.ts:223) and the getter (:234); the one test hit is an unrelated note-check helper (tests/helpers/S4B-note-check-fixture.ts:170). host.ts creates the registry (:443), passes it as `runtime` (:444) and calls only install() (:773). install() uses the private `version` counter (:235), not the getter, and no spread/Object.keys consumer exists (host.ts:443-447, :771-776).

rows.evidence: The arrow at host-settings.ts:529 is the rejection handler of `dispatchQueue = run.then(() => undefined, () => undefined)`, so it runs only if a route's operation rejects. Every fallible await in the eight routes is wrapped: directories :590-599, models/save :653-663, models/select :677-685, workspaces/open :707 (openWorkspaceImpl catches at host.ts:868-877 and :898-947) and :728-737, checks/approve :779-796 and :811-819, automation :840-848, resource-caps :876-884. The unguarded assembly calls are pure: listWorkspaces (host.ts:969-977) and buildBootstrap (host.ts:599-624) map/structuredClone already-plain data; snapshotOf :548-570 and resourceCapStatusOf :482-492 catch their probes. createHostSettings has one production assembly (host.ts:1022-1029).
rows.proposal_note: Codex's deletion is technically valid today, but the handler is the only thing that keeps dispatchQueue resolved after an unexpected throw; claude's keep-untested is the safer ruling and decision 79-4 permits it. Nothing else calls or type-depends on the handler.

Remaining hits are four test fakes (tests/app/A2-settings-automation.test.ts:27, tests/app/RL-34-wiring-resource-caps.test.ts:49, tests/app/RL-40-43-resource-cap-settings.test.ts:30, tests/work-graph/S5-notices.test.ts:76). docs/ has no listProjectIds mention, so no slice reserves it.

rows.evidence: backfillDone is either Promise.resolve() or an async IIFE (host.ts:1107-1124) whose only await, platform.workflow.backfillRecentActivity?.(...) (:1116-1117), sits inside try/catch (:1113-1122); the rest is abort checks (:1109, :1115), a plain scope literal (:1110) and a context spread (:1111). The promise cannot reject, so the close-path arrow at :1621 never runs; close() is its only reader.
rows.proposal_note: `await backfillDone;` is equivalent. If it ever rejected, close() would stop before releasing the instance lease, so keeping the one-line catch untested is the safer alternative to deleting it.

rows.evidence: probeResourceCaps is the frozen vendor API (main.ts:13). probeResourceCapsInternal wraps the probe in a .catch that returns a probe_failed capability (vendor/coding-agent/dist/sandbox/process/process-sandbox.js:2013-2024), and probeResourceCaps only maps the always-fulfilled result to .capability (:2032-2033). A synchronous throw in the default args resolveSystemdRunPath/resolveBwrapPath (:1998-2003) would escape before .catch but only reads process.env constants, so it cannot throw. The arrow at main.ts:222 never runs.
rows.proposal_note: `void probeResourceCaps();` is equivalent for the frozen vendor. Keeping the catch as a one-line guard against a vendor change (claude's option) is also fine; AGENTS rule 6 forbids editing the vendor, not deleting the caller's catch.

rows.evidence: unsupported is called at decision-actions.ts:329 (goalPhasePin undefined), :502 (goalSettings/decisionMessages undefined), :547 (decisionMessages) and :598 (goalSettings). The only builder is workflow.ts:2875-2902: it exists only when deps.goalSettings is set, always passes goalPhasePin (:2889-2899), and passes decisionMessages only when deps.decisionMessages exists (:2881-2886). The one production createWorkflow call (create-platform.ts:1887) supplies both unconditionally (goalSettings: rawGoalSettings :1854, decisionMessages: rawDecisionMessages :1855, locals at :925-927). rows.proposal_note: Class right, proposal over-reaches. Making decisionMessages required (or gating the coordinator on it) breaks tests/business/S5-decision-workflow.test.ts: its workflow is built with goalSettings and no decisionMessages (assemble at :111-122) and then expects orderGoalAdvances to return the ready ordering (:258); it would get the Workflow-level unsupported. Make goalSettings and goalPhasePin required and delete :329/:598 only; leave the :502/:547 guards (or the helper) for a supported goalSettings-without-mailbox composition, or update that test and say so.

Every adapter in the only production table returns `status: ready`: goal_conflict/applyGoalConflict (:343-390, returns :351, :374, :384, :389), command_rerun_request (:252-292, returns :259, :266, :281, :289), note_review (create-platform.ts:1641-1685, all returns ready) and unknown_call_review (create-platform.ts:1865-1874, wraps any result in ready). The table is built only from those (decision-actions.ts:406-421; create-platform.ts:1863-1877) and the only production createWorkflow uses it (create-platform.ts:1887).
